task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-19, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Opponent next-possession PPP after you run play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels; own-sequence lags similarly matter.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Is opponent next-possession PPP after play X large enough to drive AVOID labels, and what threshold defines 'large enough'?
Do own-sequence lagged outcomes add explanatory value beyond the immediate next-possession outcome?
Does deriving AVOID labels from the same possession points being tested create outcome circularity?
What sample size per play type and season is needed for stable AVOID labels?
evidence_establishes: No earlier study from this project was returned for this question, so no prior finding is established by retrieval.
The retrieval step returned zero records, so no historical result on AVOID label reliability, leakage or sample size is available.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether opponent next-possession PPP after play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels.
Any effect size, threshold, or reliability estimate for AVOID labels.
Whether earlier attempts to build or validate such labels failed or succeeded.
own_inferences: The question as posed does not define 'large enough' or the AVOID label rule, so the test cannot be run until both are fixed in advance.

If the AVOID label is built from the opponent's next-possession points, then testing whether that outcome drives the label is partly circular unless the label is defined from a separate subset of data.
Opponent next-possession outcomes depend on the opponent's lineup, the defensive matchup and the game state, so raw PPP differences are confounded by these factors.
Per-play-type, per-season samples may be small for rarer actions, which would make per-type labels noisy even at the scale of a full season.
Using lags of own-sequence outcomes adds many correlated predictors, which raises the risk of spurious findings.
uncertainties: The exact definition of AVOID, the threshold for 'large enough', and whether 'opponent next-possession' means the opponent's very next possession or the opponent's possession following the play are not specified.
The number of distinct play types X and the counts per type per season are not given.
Reliability of the derived play-type records in [source] database has not been measured in any available record.
2025-26 regular season is complete only from 2026-04-13 and the 2025-26 playoffs are partial before 2026-06-21, so the most recent data is not usable as a clean holdout on 2026-06-19.
Possible drift in play-type usage and scoring environment across 2022-23 to 2025-26 is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieval returned no records, so no historical finding changed the decision. The decision rests only on the task statement and the data description, and it reflects the undefined threshold, the outcome circularity and the sample-size and confounding issues that are visible without history.

blocking_constraints.text: AVOID labels built from the same next-possession points that are being tested make the association partly definitional unless labels are derived from separate seasons or a separate data split.
Per play-type and per-season samples may be too small to estimate PPP differences with useful precision, especially after splitting by lag and opponent context.
Opponent lineup, defensive matchup, game state and score margin affect the next-possession outcome and are not controlled in the question as posed.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved for this question, so it cannot be determined whether it has been answered. The question is not shown to be previously answered, but this is unverified because retrieval returned nothing.

risks.text: The AVOID label and the outcome being explained both come from the next-possession points, so the association may be built into the labelling rule.
If labels or lag features use possessions that occur after the play being labelled, future information leaks into the feature set.
Rarer play types and per-season splits may have too few possessions for stable PPP estimates.
Some play types may occur too infrequently per team or per opponent to reach the threshold needed for a label.
PPP of single possessions is noisy; without reliability estimates across split halves, labels may flip between seasons.
Selecting play types with extreme observed PPP and then labelling them AVOID inflates the apparent effect through regression to the mean.
Opponent quality, lineup, matchup and score-state effects are not controlled and can produce apparent PPP differences by play type.
Testing many play types, lags and thresholds creates many comparisons with no correction specified.
Errors in the play-by-play action types or sub-types, or in [source]-derived initiator and points fields, can mislabel possessions.
Possession-boundary or opponent-attribution errors in the derived records would bias the PPP estimates.
Scoring environment and play-type usage change across 2022-23 to 2025-26, so labels from one season may not hold in another.
Without a placebo such as shuffled opponent possessions, an apparent effect may reflect generic scoring variation rather than play X.

design.estimand: Difference in opponent's next-possession PPP after play X versus matched comparison plays, with own-sequence lags as secondary predictors, using a pre-specified AVOID threshold defined on a separate season.
design.unit: Possession-level records: each of the team's possessions beginning with play X, paired with the opponent's next possession.
design.sample: Derive AVOID thresholds and label rules from NBA 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular seasons only; test on NBA 2025-26 regular season after it is complete (from 2026-04-13). Exclude 2025-26 playoffs until complete (from 2026-06-21). Do not use partial data.
design.power: Before analysis, compute the number of possessions per play type needed to detect a pre-specified PPP difference at 80% power with a two-sided alpha of 0.05 after multiplicity correction; drop play types below this count rather than label them.
design.controls: Adjust for opponent team strength, score margin, period, possession start context, lineup and matchup where available; use lagged own-sequence outcomes only from possessions before play X; fit mixed models with team and opponent random effects.
design.falsification: Apply the same label rule to shuffled opponent possessions and to a play type with no expected effect; the rule should show no separation on these placebos. Re-derive labels from an independent split to check whether the label reproduces.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register the set of play types and lags; control the false discovery rate across them (e.g., Benjamini-Hochberg) and report unadjusted and adjusted results.
design.decision_rule: Classify play X as AVOID only if the pre-specified threshold is exceeded on the derivation seasons, the difference holds with the same sign on the 2025-26 regular-season holdout, it survives FDR correction, and it exceeds the placebo distribution; otherwise report uncertain or not AVOID.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs for derivation; 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13 for holdout; 2025-26 playoffs excluded until complete from 2026-06-21.
